problems.field: studies[S1].assignment.randomized and eligibility.criterion_1_random_assignment_of_ai (the conclusion under test reads S1 as a randomized experiment)
problems.form_value: Conclusion under test: people were randomly assigned to GPT-4o assistance. Final form: randomized 'not_stated', design_class 'other', criterion_1 'unclear', core 'unclear'.
problems.source_says: No sentence in PDF pp. 1-11, figures included, says how the creators were allocated to the human-only and human-AI conditions. The paper calls the design a between-subject user study with 'experimental groups' and calls the chat arm the 'treatment condition'. Neither phrase says that allocation was random, and Figure 4 shows no allocation step. The only randomization of creators is the image-topic permutation inside a condition (see confirmed). The ACM Version of Record returned HTTP 403 and was not checked. Random assignment therefore has no support in the text, and criterion 1 stays unclear, as the final form already codes it.
problems.quote: we conducted a between-subject user study with three experimental groups.
problems.locator: PDF p. 4, Section 3 (Methodology) and Section 3.1 ('treatment condition'); PDF p. 5, Figure 4; text-layer search of PDF pp. 1-11 for random*, assign*, allocat*, counterbalanc*

confirmed.statement: (a) The only randomization applied to the creators is the image-topic permutation: 'The permutation of image and topic was selected randomly but in a way that each participant used each image and each topic at most once.' It decides which three image-topic combinations a person captioned inside one condition, not which condition the person was in.

(a) 'All processing of the prompts, randomization of tasks, etc. was performed on the server' says where randomization ran, not what it covered. Figure 4 labels each human workflow 'Complete 3 Tasks', so the 'tasks' are the three image-topic combinations. The sentence does not say that condition was drawn at random.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 6, Section 3.4; PDF p. 5, Figure 4

confirmed.statement: (a) The other hits for 'random' describe outputs and recruitment, not allocation: 10 memes sampled per image-topic combination, a random 50 images per rater (Figure 5 note), and 'random users from a crowdsourcing platform'. The text layer has no hit for assign*, allocat*, counterbalanc*, or preregistration, so preregistered = not_stated is right.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 5, Section 3.2 and Figure 5; PDF p. 9, Section 5.3; text-layer search of PDF pp. 1-11

confirmed.statement: The abstract's 'three groups of 50 participants each' is not an allocation statement. The third group had no participants ('In the third group, ideas were generated fully autonomously by the LLM.'). Section 3.6 reports 124 recruited and 26 excluded for not completing, and the favorite counts (882 in total, all 441 of the collaborative condition usable, 9 per person) imply 49 per human arm. The paper gives no count at assignment, and an equal split after 26 dropouts does not show how people were allocated.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 1, Abstract; PDF p. 4, Sections 3.1 and 3.2; PDF p. 6, Section 3.6

confirmed.statement: (b) The two human arms differ in access to a generative-AI tool for the participant's own work: 'For users in the treatment condition that had access to a LLM, this part of the interface also featured a chat interface where they could prompt the LLM(Figure 3).' Ideas in the LLM's responses went into the participant's idea list automatically. Both arms are scored on memes built from the participant's own three favorites, so S1 is not a contrast in whose output gets evaluated.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 4, Sections 3.1 and 3.2; PDF p. 8, Section 5.2

confirmed.statement: (c) The tool is a large language model: 'the interaction with the OpenAI API for GPT-4o was performed by a NodeJS server.' A system prompt limited each response to at most three ideas, the current image was sent before any user prompt, and 'participants were free to enter any prompt into the system'. ai_tool.name_model (GPT-4o via the OpenAI API), role open_chat, and how_used match.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 6, Section 3.4; PDF p. 5, Section 3.3

confirmed.statement: (d) The comparison arm matches the form (ai = none, ai_vs_bau): 'The first group (baseline) participants independently generated ideas and created memes without external assistance by an AI tool or otherwise.'

(e) The design is between-person, so order randomization does not apply. Each person completed three image-topic tasks in one condition (Figure 4), and Section 5.1 compares workload 'between the two groups'. The Section 5.2 phrase 'than when they worked alone' is loose wording, not a within-person design.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 4, Section 3; PDF p. 5, Figure 4; PDF p. 8, Sections 5.1 and 5.2

confirmed.statement: The human-AI arm description is right that favorite selection and image creation had no AI: 'in the stages of idea screening and creating the meme image, no AI assistance or suggestions were provided.'

S2 is correctly coded randomized = no. No person was assigned to the AI-only condition: GPT-4o was prompted to 'generate 20 meme captions for this <image> about the topic of <topic>', and its 300 memes were sampled down to 150 and rated next to the human memes.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 4, Section 3.1; PDF p. 5, Section 3.2 and Figure 5; PDF p. 6, Section 3.3

confirmed.statement: Version: arXiv lists only v1 (20 Jan 2025) and v2 (23 Jan 2025), and v2 is the PDF on file, so no later arXiv version adds an allocation statement. The ACM Version of Record (DOI 10.1145/3708359.3712094) returned HTTP 403.
confirmed.locator: arxiv.org/abs/2501.11433, submission history; PDF p. 1, margin stamp and footnote

summary: The PDF (arXiv v2, the latest arXiv version) never says how the 98 Prolific creators were allocated to the human-only and GPT-4o chat conditions: it calls the design a 'between-subject user study with three experimental groups', and the only randomization of creators is the image-topic permutation inside a condition, so random assignment to generative-AI assistance has no support in the text and criterion 1 stays unclear. The rest of the contrast checks out (access to a GPT-4o chat panel for the participant's own captions versus no aid, between-person, so no order question), and the final form's own coding (randomized not_stated, design_class other, criterion_1 unclear) already matches the source.
